Try each question before opening its hint or answer. These practice questions
check chemical reasoning and small calculations; they are not a graded question bank.

[]{#q1}

**Q1.** Method A gives repeated values near 10.0 mg/L with SD 0.30; B gives values near 10.5 with SD 0.02. The reference is 10.0. Which is more precise, and which shows a positive mean difference?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint Q1"}
Treat spread and reference difference as separate properties.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer Q1"}
B is more precise under these repeat conditions but has an observed positive difference of about 0.5 mg/L from the reference. Good repeatability is not the same as low bias. A rigorous bias assessment would also consider reference uncertainty and design.
:::

---

[]{#q2}

**Q2.** Nine independent stable readings have sample SD 0.30 mg/L. What is the reading contribution to uncertainty in their mean?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint Q2"}
Use $s/\sqrt n$ for this specific contribution.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer Q2"}
$0.30/\sqrt9=0.10$ mg/L. Individual readings still have spread about 0.30 mg/L. The smaller mean uncertainty does not include any shared stock, preparation or sampling component.
:::

---

[]{#q3}

**Q3.** A mean has an independent reading contribution 0.03 mg/L and a shared component 0.04 mg/L. Find combined standard uncertainty.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint Q3"}
Add squared independent contributions, then take the square root.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer Q3"}
$u=\sqrt{0.03^2+0.04^2}=0.05$ mg/L. This is a standard uncertainty, not automatically a 95% interval or a complete method budget.
:::

---

[]{#q4}

**Q4.** What happens to the previous combined uncertainty if indefinitely many independent readings drive the reading component towards zero?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint Q4"}
Which component is shared by the readings?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer Q4"}
It approaches 0.04 mg/L, not zero. More readings of the same solution do not independently re-establish the shared component.
:::

---

[]{#q5}

**Q5.** Every reading has the same known +0.20 mg/L bias. Will increasing n remove it?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint Q5"}
A fixed common displacement is not independent zero-mean noise.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer Q5"}
No. The mean retains the fixed bias. Investigate or use an appropriately justified correction with its uncertainty. An arbitrary larger or smaller error bar does not itself correct the result.
:::

---

[]{#q6}

**Q6.** Two volume uncertainties arise partly from the same temperature error. Can they always be combined as independent squared terms?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint Q6"}
Shared causes can induce covariance.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer Q6"}
No. Covariance terms can matter. The independent-input square-sum formula is conditional on independence; the signs of model sensitivities and the correlations determine how shared effects propagate.
:::

---

[]{#q7}

**Q7.** A preparation has repeated identical displayed readings, so its observed SD is zero. Is the method uncertainty zero?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint Q7"}
Which sources can move every reading together without changing their scatter?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer Q7"}
No. Common calibration, preparation, recovery, display resolution and sampling effects can remain. Repeating one prepared solution does not reveal every relevant source, and zero displayed scatter is not a validation of exactness.
:::

---

[]{#q8}

**Q8.** A result is reported with standard uncertainty 0.05 mg/L. Can the reader interpret ±0.05 as a 95% interval?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint Q8"}
A coverage interpretation needs a construction and assumptions.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer Q8"}
Not from that statement alone. Standard uncertainty is on an SD-like scale. Expanded uncertainty needs a stated coverage factor and rationale; a confidence interval needs a sampling/model construction and level. State which quantity and components are included.
:::
